analysis:
Reviewed the three modified files: scripts/docs-check.sh (head lines 170-173), scripts/docs-impact-rules.json, and scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py. All are developer and CI tooling. None touches provider runtime, the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), key custody, encrypted cache storage (T-041), the fan helper or the add-on hold socket (TB-012).

docs-check.sh: the change only adds a comment about retained deleted roots in CITE_ROOTS. Behavior is unchanged. Historical-source resolution (historical_source_exists, lines 105-127) is untouched, and it still rejects paths above the repo root, Markdown targets and non-source roots.

docs-impact-rules.json: removes the "retained console" and "console protocol fixtures" rules and the console-ui telemetry-types pattern. The "provider privacy and trust" rule, which maps Security, Crypto and AppAttest sources to the threat-model and security docs (line 47-50), and the "cache storage privacy" rule (line 42-45) are unchanged. The docs-impact check that enforces threat-model doc updates for provider trust and cache code is therefore not weakened.

test-ci-component-paths.py: drops console lane expectations, fixture-sync tests and lint-console workflow tests. It adds NUL-delimited and unquoted-name routing tests, and adds console-ui/ to the forbidden strings for public workflows (including ci.yml), which tightens the check. The provider lane still covers provider-swift, libs, fixtures and the release workflows. Provider-test-gate truth-table and credential-less detector tests remain.

The patch excerpt for the test file is truncated, and the ci-component-paths.py, ci.yml and component-changes.yml implementations are not supplied. The claim that console routing was removed consistently in those files is therefore unverified. This affects CI hygiene only, not a visible security regression. No findings.
